{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABZB4I2Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhCn-zM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 21, "title": "Implement MMD_materials_outline PMX converter support, Three.js loader plugin and outline effect", "body": "## Problem

`MMD_materials_outline` now has an approved **v0.1 draft specification**, examples and independent CPU conformance fixtures, but the repository cannot yet **export PMX outline data into glTF** or **load and render outlines in Three.js**. The existing Gene Light comparison shows outlines disabled on the original PMX side and absent on the converted GLB side.

Implement the complete, reusable PMX-to-glTF outline pipeline: converter, GLTFLoader plugin, Three.js outline-rendering module, and an end-to-end browser comparison. Follow the **existing normative v0.1 draft** instead of inventing new drawing rules.

## Expected outcome

A user can convert an ordinary PMX model to GLB/glTF containing both `MMD_materials_toon` and `MMD_materials_outline`; load it into Three.js; and render its outline by registering a loader plugin and calling a dedicated effect:

```ts
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
import { MMDOutlinePlugin, MMDOutlineEffect } from './packages/three-mmd-outline';

const loader = new GLTFLoader();
loader.register(parser => new MMDOutlinePlugin(parser));
const gltf = await loader.loadAsync('model.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);

const outlineEffect = new MMDOutlineEffect(renderer);
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => {
  outlineEffect.render(scene, camera); // replaces renderer.render(scene, camera)
});
```

This is the **target API shape**, not an assertion that the symbols exist today. It should be straightforward to use *alongside* the existing `MMDToonPlugin`, without forcing an app to use toon shading. Define integration and disposal behavior explicitly.

## Relevant existing code and specification

- Authoritative draft for **this implementation**: [`extensions/MMD_materials_outline/README.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/extensions/MMD_materials_outline/README.md), updated by [Issue #19](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/issues/19) / [PR #20](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/pull/20); its [CPU conformance fixtures](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/tree/main/extensions/MMD_materials_outline/tests).
- Existing PMX converter: [`tools/pmx-to-gltf.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/tools/pmx-to-gltf.ts), uses `mmd-parser` and glTF Transform; already exposes PMX material `flag`, `edgeColor`, `edgeSize`, and saves those values in `extras`, but does not output the outline extension. The PMX vertex type needs the parsed `edgeRatio` field.
- Existing toon GLTFLoader plugin: [`packages/three-mmd-toon/`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/tree/main/packages/three-mmd-toon). Its material loader must continue working unmodified in meaning when both extensions are present.
- Existing Three.js reference: [`three-mmd-loader/src/effects/MMDOutlineEffect.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/src/effects/MMDOutlineEffect.ts) offers an example of rendering an inverted hull through `WebGPURenderer`/TSL's render-object hook. This module is **not** the glTF outline specification, is tied to `MMDToonMaterial`, and uses a different thickness law. Do not simply copy its shader constants.
- Current Gene Light comparison: [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts); the left reference uses published `@takahirox/three-mmd@0.1.2`, the right uses the generated GLB and toon/PBR toggle. The site uses one renderer, camera, and scissored panes.

## Implementation scope

### 1. PMX-to-glTF conversion

- Preserve PMX material edge flag `0x10`: include `materials[i].extensions.MMD_materials_outline` **only** when enabled. Write `colorFactor` = source `edgeColor` and `sizeFactor` = source `edgeSize` unchanged (no unit scaling or color compensation), using the documented defaults where omitted. Add `MMD_materials_outline` to `extensionsUsed`, not `extensionsRequired` for the normal PBR fallback.
- Read each parsed PMX vertex's **`edgeRatio`** and write the optional `_MMD_EDGE_SCALE` `SCALAR/FLOAT` attribute on primitives using the extension; values are finite **and may be signed**. Omit the attribute only when all applicable values are exactly 1, meaning the shader must then use the specified default 1.0. A zero ratio is not an absent ratio. Handle shared vertex accessors and material face groups correctly; do not multiply the source ratio by material size in storage.
- Add a focused glTF Transform writer for the outline extension alongside the existing toon writer, preserving independent extension declarations and PBR fallback. Do not create a duplicated/expanded mesh in the asset. Keep existing geometry, scale, textures, core alpha classification and metadata intact.
- Validate output with the Khronos glTF Validator plus extension-specific schema/data checks. Expand converter tests for edge flag on/off, defaults, nonuniform ratios, zero and negative scales, multiple materials, extension coexistence, GLB and `.gltf` output, and round-trip attribute payload verification.

### 2. Three.js GLTFLoader plugin

- Implement a reusable TypeScript `MMDOutlinePlugin` with `name = 'MMD_materials_outline'`. Inspect the GLTFLoader parser's supported lifecycle hooks; use the appropriate hook(s) to preserve/validate `_MMD_EDGE_SCALE`, associate parsed material payloads with the **correct nodes/primitives/material groups**, and pass those records to the renderer. Do **not** replace standard/PBR materials in order to attach outlines.
- Independently validate material payloads, `extensionsUsed`/required semantics, accessor component type/count/normalized/sparse rules, positions/normals, primitive topology and finite source values. Reuse the fixtures in `extensions/MMD_materials_outline/tests`. Fail clearly with context on invalid assets; do not silently repair them.
- Outline support must work with **core PBR only**, with the separate **MMDToonPlugin**, and with other compatible materials if a documented material-factor-alpha integration is supplied. Do not read Toon fields unless that material is actively using Toon; do not alter other extensions or their fallback behavior.
- Provide an explicit disposal path for created resources and loaded-scene metadata, with no stale shared-geometry mutation or leaking renderer hooks.

### 3. Three.js MMDOutlineEffect

- Implement `MMDOutlineEffect(renderer)` exposing `render(scene,camera)` in a reusable module, with documented lifecycle/disposal, compatible with Three.js r186's `WebGPURenderer` on its **WebGL2 TSL backend** and native WebGPU when available.
- Render an additional inverted-hull pass **from the original geometry**, independent of the source material subclass. Respect mesh instances, material groups, visibility, source transforms, morph/skinning, front-face culling, `LESS_EQUAL`, depth writes **enabled**, no depth bias, and the extension's unlit color and skip rules. Avoid triangle sorting and avoid applying the legacy three-mmd thickness formula.
- Implement the **exact v0.1 provisional clip-space equation**: `e=sizeFactor*vertexScale`, use view-space transformed normal XY, normalize with specified zero case, offset clip XY by `clip.w*(2*e*n.xy/viewport.xy)`, without additional scaling or clamps. Use the **actual active pane/viewport size in render-target pixels** (important for the side-by-side scissor demo). Verify perspective/orthographic cameras, normal matrices, signed scales and relevant degeneracies against the numerical fixtures.
- Implement material-factor alpha as chapter 6 specifies: suppress when active material's **diffuse factor alpha is exactly zero**; otherwise use independent `colorFactor.a`, including for partially transparent edges. Support core `baseColorFactor[3]` and active toon `diffuseFactor[3]`, plus a documented integration for other material models. Do not conflate this with final texture alpha/alphaMode. Keep zero size, zero edge alpha and all-zero edge scale skip semantics correct.
- **Important compatibility challenge:** the draft requires **encoded/gamma-domain straight-alpha source-over**, including partially transparent outlines, while Three.js ordinarily composites in linear light. Implement a correct WebGL2 rendering/compositing strategy (for example a dedicated appropriate offscreen/resolve pass, if necessary), preserving the source's RGB domain exactly and preventing extra sRGB conversions. Merely setting `transparent=true` is not sufficient evidence of correctness. Scope the strategy to what this outline module needs; do not change ordinary base-material/PBR/toon output.
- Prove actual GPU behavior using readback/pixel measurements for opaque backgrounds and semitransparent edge RGB with a discriminating midgray case (`encoded 0.5` edge at `alpha 0.5` over encoded black must output about `0.25`, not linear-light `~0.36`). Test blending, alpha suppression, depth/occlusion, material group layering, nonuniform transform and viewport dimensions. State numeric tolerances and rendering settings. This is a **mandatory conformance check**, not optional if it proves difficult.

### 4. Gene Light comparison demo and documentation

- Extend the existing pinned Gene Light generation to produce a GLB with `MMD_materials_outline` and its per-vertex scales. Preserve hash-verified source model, asset terms/notices, metadata and other extensions.
- Expose a simple **outline on/off** option in the demo, allowing outline rendering on the GLB right pane and a comparable original-PMX outline using `@takahirox/three-mmd` on the left. Clearly label when the two sides use different outline algorithms or appearance. Preserve static rest pose, synchronized orbit/zoom, front/side/back, toon/PBR toggle, one renderer/scissored panes and mobile layout.
- Capture browser-rendered front/side/back comparisons, actually inspect them for obvious missing/overdrawn outlines, incorrect thickness, black spots or view-dependent artifacts, and document findings and remaining limitations. Do not claim exact original MMD fidelity from a comparison against another renderer.
- Update README, pipeline/plugin instructions, usage examples and relevant validation records with the public API and reproducible commands. No need to modify the official draft merely to simplify implementation; bring any confirmed spec contradictions to review rather than silently deviating.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] PMX converter emits conformant `MMD_materials_outline` data and valid custom vertex attributes, preserving signed PMX values and the independent `MMD_materials_toon` + PBR paths; glTF Validator reports zero core errors.
- [ ] A public, documented `GLTFLoader.register(...MMDOutlinePlugin...)` + `new MMDOutlineEffect(renderer)` / `effect.render(scene,camera)` API works. The loader plugin and effect are independent of the MMDToon material class.
- [ ] The production TSL/WebGL2 outline path matches the **current normative v0.1 fixtures** (projection, signed/default/zero edge scales, clipping, culling, depth, base-factor-alpha rules), not just code that produces visible black lines.
- [ ] **Encoded/gamma-domain alpha blending** passes independent browser pixel tests, including a case distinguishing it from conventional linear compositing. Proper visibility and depth ordering on partially transparent edges are tested.
- [ ] Core PBR-only, MMD toon + outline, optional-extension fallback and other-material integration behaviors are tested without changing the existing toon numerical conformance expectations.
- [ ] The built Gene Light demo renders both the direct PMX reference and new glTF outline, permits toggling outlines and toon/PBR, and passes matched-view browser checks with no asset/network/shader/runtime errors. Visual evidence is actually reviewed.
- [ ] Existing `npm run test:outline`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links` and `git diff --check` pass as applicable. Document actual execution results, skips and environment limitations.
- [ ] Changes are limited to outline converter/plugin/rendering support, relevant example/tests/docs, and justified supporting code. No unrelated new MMD extensions, speculative framework changes or arbitrary deviation from v0.1.

## Optional validation

- Native WebGPU testing where a real adapter is available. No adapter is a documented skip, not a blocker if WebGL2 mandatory checks pass.
- Additional synthetic skinned/morphed test models or a larger PMX with varied edge settings, beyond the mandatory focused fixtures.

## Required post-merge verification

After merging into `main` and the GitHub Pages deployment, confirm at https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/ that both views render, outline on/off and toon/PBR toggles work, required assets/notices load, and the browser has no shader/runtime/network errors. Record workflow URL, deployed commit and actual outcome. These publication-only checks remain **post-merge**.
